items.title: Airbnb pledges $500M for its nonprofit to offer more free emergency stays
items.summary: Airbnb plans to dedicate $500 million to its nonprofit Airbnb.org over five years to expand free temporary housing for medical travelers and disaster survivors. Funding will come from 10 cents per booking, with Airbnb covering any shortfall, and the goal is 1 million free nights a year.

items.title: Nonprofits look for a reset following the midterms
items.summary: Chronicle reporting says nonprofit leaders hope a Democratic-led Congress will restore federal grant flows halted or paused under the Trump administration. Independent Sector's Akilah Watkins cited priorities including research, human services, education, and nutrition assistance.

items.title: Children’s hospital scores $200 million in gifts from two couples
items.summary: Ben and Felicia Horowitz gave $150 million to Intermountain Health to build Nevada's first standalone children's hospital, to be named for them. Larry and Heidi Canarelli committed $50 million to the same planned southwest Las Vegas hospital, which is scheduled to open in 2030.

items.title: Nonprofits and others step in as disaster aid becomes a political lottery
items.summary: The Trump administration denied 26 percent of major disaster declarations in 2025, more than double the prior year's rate. A study found approvals were far higher for all-Republican states than all-Democratic states, and Michigan's aid requests were denied twice after 2026 tornadoes.

items.title: A food bank targeted donors based on their politics. Here’s what they learned.
items.summary: The Food Bank of Central & Eastern North Carolina tailored fundraising appeals to donors' political affiliations to raise money after federal funding losses. The article says an increasing share of nonprofits are taking this approach to match messages to political leanings.

items.title: Funding When Democracy Is in Decline (Blog)

items.title: How new tech billionaires can save more lives
items.summary: A Chronicle opinion piece argues effective altruism donors could save more lives by funding policy change, citing estimates of under $5 per life saved for trans fat advocacy. It notes a new generation of tech donors may give tens of billions annually.

items.title: ‘AI recommends, humans decide’: Circle Foundation’s bet on agentic philanthropy
items.summary: The Chronicle reports that the Circle Foundation, founded a little over a year ago from 1 percent of shares in Circle Internet Group, plans to delegate most grantmaking functions to AI agents with no more than two human employees. It plans quarterly in-person reporting calls and a donor-advised fund.

items.title: After the midterms, democracy funders must not take their foot off the gas
